text:
maria: Heads-up — since last night's driver rollout to 546.1 on eu-west GPUs we're seeing a small but sustained bump in Xid errors and NCCL watchdog timeouts in a subset of pods. Not a full outage yet but noisy.
raj: saw that alert at 01:12, investigating. Which clusters specifically?
maria: eu-west-prod-gpu and eu-west-batch-1. Mostly p3/p4 pools, tail latencies up ~2-3x on some jobs.
cheng: deploy-bot shows the driver rollout completed at 00:45 across eu-west.
deploy-bot: driver-rollout: version=546.1 region=eu-west status=successful started=1787999500 finished=1788000300
sre-oncall: jumping in. I pulled nvml logs from one affected node, there are repeated Xid 31 and Xid 43 messages around 00:50-01:05.
leo: Xid 31 is memory access fault, Xid 43 is illegal instruction in some driver paths. Could be a kernel+driver ABI mismatch on a handful of hosts.
raj: can we correlate with kernel versions? I remember the kernel bump last week on eu-west-hosts-2.
maria: yes — eu-west-hosts-2 have kernel 6.3.4-rt, other hosts at 6.2.x. The driver rollback test on a host with 6.2 didn't reproduce.
cheng: that suggests a compatibility regression with kernel 6.3.4-rt + 546.1. We should update runbook to include kernel check for Xid spikes.
sre-oncall: Quick mitigation: cordon affected nodes, drain GPU pods onto nodes still on 6.2, and create a canary pool that pins driver to 545.3 for kernel 6.3 hosts.
leo: I can prepare a short kube job to evict pods and move batch jobs — want to avoid preempting inference traffic.
raj: Please add/patch an alert: increase sensitivity for "nvidia.xid.rate" so we get per-node spikes (not only global). Current rule is global > 50/min which hides small clusters of failures.
maria: agreed. Proposed alert:
```
- alert: NvidiaXIDNodeSpike
  expr: rate(nvidia_gpu_nvml_xid_total[1m]) > 0.5
  for: 2m
  labels:
    severity: warning
  annotations:
    summary: "XID spike on node {{ $labels.instance }}"
```
cheng: I recommend we scope by driver_version and kernel_version labels so we can auto-assign to infra owners: severity=critical if driver==546.1 and kernel>=6.3
sre-oncall: adding checklist to thread (short playbook):
 1) Identify nodes with Xid > 5 in 5m (promql below).
 2) Check kernel_version and driver_version via inventory service.
 3) If driver==546.1 && kernel>=6.3 -> cordon + drain, pin to 545.3; else cordon + restart nvidia-dcgm + kubelet.
 4) If tasks are latency-sensitive, route traffic to fallback region (eu-central) using traffic-router.
 5) If drain fails due to unschedulable pods, fallback: restart driver on node and monitor for 10m.
PromQL example to find nodes:
```
sum by(node, driver_version, kernel_version) (increase(nvidia_gpu_nvml_xid_total[5m]))
```
maria: nice. Also add a dashboard panel for "NCCL watchdog timeouts" using metric nccl_watchdog_timeouts_total so we can spot correlation.
leo: I'll add a Grafana panel and a runbook section to link to the node inventory + kernel tag.
raj: action items: leo to add dashboard and alert patch (ETA 2h), cheng to prepare a pinning daemonset image (545.3) and a rollback playbook (ETA 3h), maria to update runbook text and incident doc (ETA 1h). I'm on-call to coordinate.
cheng: I'll also add a smoke test job that runs a small NCCL all-reduce across a canary node after driver change. Automate it into our rollout pipeline.
sre-oncall: temporary pager-rule: escalate Xid spike alerts if >10 nodes affected across a region. For now keep as warning to avoid noisy pages.
maria: thanks — one more: add a quick command snippet to runbook for manual repro on node:
```
# on node
sudo systemctl stop kubelet
sudo modprobe -r nvidia_uvm nvidia
sudo modprobe nvidia
sudo systemctl start kubelet
# run tiny NCCL job from infra tools
infra-nccl-run --gpus 2 --iters 20
```
raj: good. Capture outputs to /var/log/nvidia-repro.log and include a parsing helper in the runbook.
leo: I'll drop the updated runbook link here once uploaded.
maria: great work — this should keep us ahead of noisy regressions during driver rollouts. We'll revisit after the dashboard + alert changes. :thumbsup:
